title: Faster approximate dynamic distances on monotone grids
formal: Can (1+ε)-approximate opposite-corner distances in a weighted directed square grid be supported with offline-known weight updates at polylogarithmic amortized update cost and square-root query cost?
definitions:
Choose h≥2, N=h², and the directed grid on [h]² with every east, north and northeast arc that stays in the grid. Source is (1,1) and target (h,h). Every arc has an integer weight in [0,N^a] for any fixed positive integer a. An update replaces one arc weight by another allowed value; topology stays fixed. Let ε∈(0,1] be rational with O(log N) bits. A distance query returns a rational d_hat satisfying d≤d_hat≤(1+ε)d, so zero distances must be answered exactly. No path report is required.

The complete list of U weight updates, including new values, is supplied before initialization. Queries are requested as the update list is replayed; their placement is not known in advance. Use a deterministic word-RAM with O(log(N+U+2)) bits per word, with a constant large enough for the weight bound, and polynomially many words. There must be absolute exponents c,d and a polynomial P such that preparing the initial graph and all update-list data takes at most P(N,1/ε)+U ε^(−d)log^c(N+U+2) time, and subsequent replay costs at most U ε^(−d)log^c(N+U+2) in total for updates and ε^(−d)sqrt(N)log^c(N+U+2) worst-case time per query. No additional polynomial-in-U preprocessing term is allowed. Bounds are for every U, not only short sequences; time spent precomputing future distances counts toward preparation.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked algorithm and proof of all stated guarantees, or prove the precise target impossible. State any complexity hypothesis used in a conditional impossibility.
context: The DTW paper uses offline planar-distance tradeoffs and asks for better approximate dynamic grid bounds. Arbitrary polynomial preprocessing in the whole sequence would make the intended target vacuous.
why: The proposed tradeoff connects dynamic geometric distances to faster approximate time-series alignment.

import_provenance.original_title: Faster approximate dynamic distances on monotone grids
import_provenance.original_statement: For a directed N-vertex grid with east, north and northeast arcs and nonnegative weights, can fixed opposite-corner distances be maintained within 1+ε with polylog(N)·poly(1/ε) update time and √N polylog(N)·poly(1/ε) query time? Allow polynomial preprocessing and an offline-known sequence of arbitrary weight changes.
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: Editorial benchmark sharpening the paper’s explicit dynamic-grid question; its reduction would yield near-quadratic approximate DTW under translation. Approximation is essential here: exact dynamic planar-distance tradeoffs face conditional lower bounds.

context_blocks.text: The DTW paper uses offline planar-distance tradeoffs and asks for better approximate dynamic grid bounds. Arbitrary polynomial preprocessing in the whole sequence would make the intended target vacuous.

sentences: The graph is a square grid with only monotone directed arcs.
All update values are known in advance but query placement is not.
Preprocessing cannot hide superlinear work in the update count.
The target combines polylogarithmic update work with square-root distance-query time.
